newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht eases late, interbank rate falls.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht eases late, interbank rate falls.

text.p: The Thai baht weakened against the dollar in late trade on Monday on rising commercial demand for the U.S. unit, dealers said.
"The dollar was quiet well bid on some strong commercial demand," said one dealer at foreign bank. "But the interbank trade remained quiet as offshore parties were still ruled out."

The baht was traded at 25.810/25.840 to the dollar late in local market against 25.790/25.810 early. In the offshore market, the baht was traded at around 25.660/25.760 compared with 25.803/25.818 earlier.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the mid-rate at 25.78 per dollar versus 25.79 on Friday.

The baht/dollar forex market is informally divided into offshore and local markets since the central bank's move to cut off offshore players' access to the baht at the middle of this month when the currency was attacked by speculators.

Dealers said the economic datas released by the Bank of Thailand on Monday had no impact on the baht as figures were mostly in line with market expectations. Others said it was over optimistic given current woes faced by the Thai economy.
The one-month baht-dollar swap premium was traded at 45/65 satangs per dollar late compared with 50/70 earlier.
The overnight interbank rate declined to 12.00-13.00 percent early from 14.00/15.00 in the morning on central bank's liquidity injection through its bond repurchase market operation, dealers said.
